+    def _is_all_or_any_call(self, call):
+        """Check if a call node is calling all() or any()."""
+        return (
+            isinstance(call.func, ast.Name)
+            and call.func.id in ("all", "any")
+            and len(call.args) == 1
+            and not call.keywords
+        )
+
+    def _unroll_all_any(self, call):
+        """
+        Unroll all() or any() calls with comprehensions.
+        
+        Returns (unrolled_node, explanation) if the call can be unrolled,
+        or None if it cannot be unrolled (in which case the default behavior is used).
+        """
+        if not self._is_all_or_any_call(call):
+            return None
+        
+        func_name = call.func.id
+        arg = call.args[0]
+        
+        # Check if the argument is a comprehension
+        if not isinstance(arg, (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp, ast.SetComp)):
+            # For other iterables, we can't easily unroll them
+            return None
+        
+        # We only handle single-level comprehensions for now
+        if len(arg.generators) != 1:
+            return None
+        
+        comp = arg.generators[0]
+        
+        # We don't handle comprehensions with conditions for now
+        if comp.ifs:
+            return None
+        
+        # Extract the element expression and the loop variable
+        elt = arg.elt
+        target = comp.target
+        iter_expr = comp.iter
+        
+        # Create a variable to hold the iterable
+        iter_var = self.variable()
+        self.statements.append(
+            ast.Assign([ast.Name(iter_var, ast.Store())], iter_expr)
+        )
+        
+        # Create a variable to hold the result
+        result_var = self.variable()
+        
+        # Initialize the result variable
+        if func_name == "all":
+            # For all(), initialize to True
+            self.statements.append(
+                ast.Assign([ast.Name(result_var, ast.Store())], _NameConstant(True))
+            )
+        else:  # func_name == "any"
+            # For any(), initialize to False
+            self.statements.append(
+                ast.Assign([ast.Name(result_var, ast.Store())], _NameConstant(False))
+            )
+        
+        # Create the loop body
+        loop_body = []
+        
+        # Visit the element expression to get its value and explanation
+        elt_res, elt_expl = self.visit(elt)
+        
+        # Store the result
+        loop_body.append(
+            ast.Assign([ast.Name(result_var, ast.Store())], elt_res)
+        )
+        
+        if func_name == "all":
+            # For all(), break if any element is falsy
+            negation = ast.UnaryOp(ast.Not(), elt_res)
+            loop_body.append(ast.If(negation, [ast.Break()], []))
+        else:  # func_name == "any"
+            # For any(), break if any element is truthy
+            loop_body.append(ast.If(elt_res, [ast.Break()], []))
+        
+        # Create the for loop
+        for_loop = ast.For(
+            target,
+            ast.Name(iter_var, ast.Load()),
+            loop_body,
+            []
+        )
+        
+        self.statements.append(for_loop)
+        
+        # Return the result variable
+        return ast.Name(result_var, ast.Load()), elt_expl
+
